newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end flat.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices stalled around unchanged late on Friday while traders waited to see whether the Federal Reserve will decide to raise interest rates when its policy makers meet on Tuesday.
With the consensus among market participants tilted towards a 25-basis point increase, traders speculated about how much of this expectation already was built into prices.
Should the central bank follow this scenario, prices likely would quickly turn down, but that might prompt bargain-hunters to step into the fray.
"I think they expect it to happen, they expect the market to trade off, and will buy a dip," one trader said.
However, the market might not draw bottom-fishers if it decides that this latest rate rise will be followed by others, he added.
"That's the real issue, if they think the Federal Reserve is acting in premptively, they should like it. If they think this is a sucession of rate moves, the market won't like it."

While only a minority now seem to favor the possibility that the central bank will opt to leave rates unchanged, traders said such a decision likely would soothe anxious traders, at least in the near-term. As a result, it probably would inspire them to bid prices up.
But until Tuesday, traders speculated that the market might remain trapped in the doldrums, noting that a number of players are expected to be out on Monday as it a Jewish holiday.

December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade ended four ticks higher at 112-20/32 ticks. Traders attributed the firmer tone to local trading, noting institutions were conspicuous by their absence.
The December Treasury futures edged up three ticks to 107-24/32. The MOB spread stood at 156 ticks, slightly firmer than at midday.

Among the issues that were actively traded, Dade County Florida Water and Sewer System Revenues of 2025, which have a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 5.82 percent on a net basis, off three basis points from levels seen on Thursday.
But Matagorda County, Texas, District Number One pollution control bonds of 2030, which have a 6-1/8 percent coupon, were bid at 100-1/2, up from the 100-1/8 level seen on Thursday.
